paragraphs.text: The most common modern beehive is built from a stack of wooden boxes. At the bottom is a floor with an entrance slot, through which the bees fly in and out.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The lowest box, called the brood box, is where the queen lays her eggs and young bees develop. Above it, beekeepers place a flat metal grid known as a queen excluder. Its gaps are wide enough for worker bees to pass through but too narrow for the larger queen.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The boxes above the excluder are called supers. Because the queen cannot reach them, the bees fill these boxes only with honey, which the beekeeper can harvest without disturbing the eggs.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: A crown board covers the top box, and a sloping roof keeps out the rain.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Beekeepers usually inspect a hive every week in spring and summer, wearing protective clothing and using gentle smoke to keep the bees calm while the boxes are open.
paragraphs.label: E
